newsitem.title: UK: SmithKline says Medicare allegations unproved.
newsitem.headline: SmithKline says Medicare allegations unproved.

text.p: Drugs giant SmithKline Beecham Plc said on Friday that allegations it falsely billed the U.S. federally-funded Medicare program remain "unproved".
A company spokesman declined to comment on a report that SmithKline Beecham is close to an agreement to pay the U.S. government more than $300 million following the launch of a federal investigation.

"Smithkline Beecham stands on its record as an ethical company," he told Reuters. "As previously announced we have been actively working to resolve a government investigation of which these unproved allegations are a part."

The Wall Street Journal reported on Friday that a settlement is expected in the next two months. It said the exact nature of the investigation had not been disclosed, but is believed to involve SmithKline Beecham's clinical laboratory unit.
The report said the unit is suspected of charging Medicare for unnecessary blood tests and other laboratory work.
SmithKline Beecham shares were down 3p at 764.5 by 0930 GMT.
